Title: Photocatalytic hydrogen evolution on doped titanium dioxide
Abstract: Titanium dioxide nanoparticles doped with nitrogen and copper were synthesized by a sol-gel route and characterized by X-ray diffraction, transmission electron microscopy and UV-visible spectroscopy. Doping narrowed the band gap and increased visible-light absorption. Photocatalytic hydrogen production under simulated sunlight improved threefold compared with undoped samples, and the catalyst remained stable over ten reuse cycles.

Title: Soil carbon response to long-term crop rotation
Abstract: Soil organic carbon, microbial biomass and nitrogen mineralization were measured across twenty years of crop rotation experiments in semi-arid farmland. Legume rotations increased soil carbon stocks and enzyme activity relative to continuous wheat. Reduced tillage further limited erosion and nutrient leaching, suggesting rotation management can improve soil fertility and sequester atmospheric carbon.

Title: Gene regulation by a conserved transcription factor in zebrafish
Abstract: We identify a conserved transcription factor that regulates heart regeneration in zebrafish. Using chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing and CRISPR knockouts, we show that the factor binds enhancers of cardiac genes after injury. Loss of the protein impaired cardiomyocyte proliferation and delayed tissue repair, revealing a molecular mechanism that links gene expression to regenerative capacity.

Title: Seismic wave attenuation in the upper crust
Abstract: Seismograms recorded by a dense array in a tectonically active region were analysed to estimate seismic wave attenuation in the upper crust. Quality factors were inverted for different frequency bands and compared with lithology and fault geometry. Low quality factors coincide with fractured zones and fluid-saturated sediments, providing constraints for earthquake hazard modelling.

Title: Existence of solutions to a nonlinear elliptic equation
Abstract: We prove the existence and uniqueness of weak solutions to a class of nonlinear elliptic partial differential equations with variable exponents. Using variational methods and the mountain pass theorem, we establish regularity results and derive a priori estimates. Several examples illustrate that the assumptions on the nonlinearity cannot be relaxed.

Title: Brand trust and repurchase intention in online retail
Abstract: This study investigates how brand trust, service quality and customer satisfaction influence repurchase intention in online retail. Survey data from 480 consumers were analysed using structural equation modelling. Results show that trust mediates the effect of service quality on loyalty, and that personalized marketing strengthens customer retention and long-term firm revenue.

Title: Board diversity and firm financial performance
Abstract: We examine whether board gender diversity and director independence affect the financial performance of listed firms. Using panel data on 1,200 companies over ten years, we find that diverse boards are associated with higher return on assets and lower earnings management. The effects are stronger in firms with weaker shareholder protection and higher information asymmetry.

Title: Supply chain resilience in manufacturing companies
Abstract: This paper explores how manufacturing firms build supply chain resilience after major disruptions. Interviews and survey data from procurement managers show that supplier diversification, inventory buffers and digital visibility improve operational performance. Firms that combine collaborative supplier relationships with flexible logistics strategies recover faster and reduce costs during demand uncertainty.

Title: Entrepreneurial orientation and startup growth
Abstract: Drawing on resource-based theory, we study how entrepreneurial orientation, access to venture capital and managerial experience shape the growth of technology startups. A sample of 320 new ventures indicates that innovativeness and proactive market strategy raise revenue growth, while limited funding weakens the effect of risk-taking on profitability.

Title: Gender inequality and rural women's employment
Abstract: This research examines how gender inequality and unequal access to education shape employment outcomes for young women in rural communities. Interviews with 120 households reveal that cultural norms, family expectations and limited childcare restrict social mobility despite recent policy reforms. We discuss implications for community development and education policy.

Title: Migrant integration and sense of belonging
Abstract: We study the experiences of migrant families adapting to a new society, focusing on identity, language and community support. Qualitative interviews and ethnographic observation show that discrimination and weak welfare provision hinder integration and sense of belonging among second-generation youth, while local civic associations offer important social networks.

Title: Political participation among ethnic minorities
Abstract: The article analyses political participation and trust in local government among ethnic minority groups. Survey results indicate that civic engagement is strongly associated with neighbourhood networks and perceived discrimination. Inclusive governance policies and community organizations increase democratic legitimacy and participation in local elections.

Title: Family structure and educational attainment
Abstract: Using longitudinal survey data, we investigate how family structure, parental education and household income influence children's educational attainment. Children in single-parent households show lower attainment on average, but strong community support and school resources reduce the gap. The findings inform social welfare and education policy.

Title: Climate policy, carbon taxes and household inequality
Abstract: This study examines how carbon taxes affect household energy consumption and income inequality across regions. Combining survey data with an energy demand model, we find that carbon pricing is regressive without compensation, while targeted rebates protect low-income households. The results inform climate policy design and social equity.

Title: Machine learning model to predict customer churn
Abstract: A machine learning framework is developed to predict customer churn in telecommunication companies using usage, billing and service data. Random forest and gradient boosting models are compared, and feature importance analysis identifies contract type and support calls as key drivers. The model supports targeted retention strategies and customer relationship management.

Title: Retrieval-augmented generation for question answering
Abstract: Large pre-trained language models store factual knowledge in their parameters, but their ability to access and update it is limited. We combine a pre-trained sequence-to-sequence generator with a dense retriever over Wikipedia, and fine-tune the system end to end. The approach sets new results on open-domain question answering tasks.
